summary: Cowlitz County, WA: lookout tower of 1930 replaced in 1936 and 1940; Jake Nordvik staffed it; blown down and abandoned about 1968; site gone; access by permit.

facts.design: 60' pole tower with cab and living quarters (1930); 57' per 1930 newspaper; 60' hewn cedar tower (1936); 30' live-in tower (1940)
facts.status_note: Abandoned about 1968 after the tower was blown down (Willhite); Register and firelookout.com say abandoned 1968 and gone

access.note: Roads reach within the last half mile; Willhite says a St. Helens Tree Farm Permit is needed to use them legally

visit.trail_note: Final trail is a decommissioned road that climbs steeply from a high parking lot (Willhite)

events.note: First known lookout person placed on the peak (Willhite); a crow's nest temporary lookout had been erected around 1927-28 (Forest Lookouts)
60 ft pole tower with cab and living quarters (Register). A 1930 newspaper and Willhite give 57 ft
Hewn cedar tower, sixty feet high, erected after an older white fir tower became dangerous (1936 annual report). Willhite's photo caption gives 66 ft
Jake Nordvik, lookout for 11 years per a December 1937 story; firelookout.com lists him 1927?-1947
Tower fell in the winter of 1939
Replacement live-in tower: 30 ft (Register), 30 ft treated timber L-4 (firelookout.com), 29 ft ring-connected with ground house (Willhite quoting a state report)
Aircraft Warning Service used the site for a period (Willhite)
George Stanford listed as lookout (firelookout.com); other names listed through 1954
Tower damaged in the Columbus Day storm
Martin Burrows, aged 18, was the lookout; reached by a three-mile hike with no electricity or phone (Willhite)
Abandoned in 1968 (Register, firelookout.com). Willhite says blown down and abandoned around 1968
Registered April 7, 2020; nominated by Tammy McLeod

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 60 ft; the 1930 newspaper and Willhite give 57 ft. Willhite's photo caption gives the 1936 tower 66 ft, and the 1936 annual report gives 60 ft. The story reports these as written.
The 1936 annual report describes an earlier white fir tower built a decade before 1936, which does not match the Register's 1930 date. The story reports both without choosing.
Register and firelookout.com give 30 ft for the 1940 tower; Willhite quotes a state report giving 29 ft.
The 1937 Forest Log story quoted by Forest Lookouts places Elk Mountain in Lewis County; the Register and Willhite place it in Cowlitz County.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 17.4 matches the 57 ft figure from the 1930 newspaper; the Register and firelookout.com give 60 ft, so height_m is set to 18.3. Brief access 'unknown' is better recorded as permission per Willhite. Dates and heights conflict across sources (1930 vs earlier white fir tower; 57/60/66 ft). County conflict (Lewis vs Cowlitz) noted. Willhite photo captions not used beyond the 66 ft caption. Brief events (1930 built, 2020 registration) are supported.
